text: Problem set 3 Problem 1. Let Qn(1) = {f ∈ Pn(R) : f (1) = 0} be as in Homework 2 Problem 3. (i) Show that Pn(R) = Qn(1) ⊕ span(1). (ii) Describe the quotient space Pn(R)/Qn(1) (what does a typical coset look like?). (iii) Determine dim(Pn(R)/Qn(1)). You can use any results that were proved in Homework 2 Problem 3. Problem 2. Let V be a vector space and V1, V2, U be subspaces such that V = V1 ⊕U = V2 ⊕ U . Is it true that V1 = V2? If yes, prove it. If no, give an example. Problem 3. Let T : V → W be a linear transformation between vector spaces V, W . (i) Let x ∈ span(v1, . . . , vn). Show that T (x) ∈ span(T (v1), . . . , T (vn)). (ii) Let U ⊂ V be a subspace. Show that T (U ) is a subspace of W . (iii) If v1, . . . , vn ∈ V is linearly dependent, then T (v1), . . . , T (vn) is linearly depen- dent. (iv) If T (v1), . . . , T (vn) is linearly independent, then v1, . . . , vn ∈ V is linearly inde- pendent. (v) Give an example of T and v1, . . . , vn ∈ V where v1, . . . , vn is linearly independent but T (v1), . . . , T (vn) is linearly dependent. Problem 4. Show that the following maps are linear transformations. (i) Let W ⊂ V be a subspace. The canonical projection π : V → V /W is given by π(x) = x + W . (ii) Let W ⊂ V be a subspace. The inclusion map ι : W → V is given by ι(x) = x for x ∈ W . (iii) Let V be the vector space in Homework 1 Problem 1. We define T : V → C(R) by T (f )(x) = log(f (x)). (iv) Let V be the vector space in Homework 1 Problem 1. We define S : C(R) → V by S(f )(x) = ef (x). (v) We define T : Pn(R) → Pn(R) by T (p)(x) = p(x + 1) which means we replace x by x + 1 in the polynomial. For example T (x2 + 1) = (x + 1)2 + 1 = x2 + 2x + 2. 1
